content.title: About
content.content: A cookie brownie without icing is a soft dessert that combines a crisp cookie crust with the dense, moist texture of classic brownie. Made without any frosting, it retains the natural chocolate flavor with a hint of vanilla.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brownies originated in the United States in the early 20th century and quickly became popular for their simplicity and rich taste.
The cookie‑brownie combination creates a contrast of textures: a crunchy outer layer and a tender interior.
Without icing the dessert contains less added sugar, making it a slightly lighter option for those watching sweetness intake.
Traditional recipes use dark chocolate, which is rich in antioxidants.
Cookie brownies are often served in bite‑size portions, ideal for a snack or after‑lunch treat.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Dark chocolate in the brownie provides flavonoids that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The mix of carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat offers a quick boost of energy.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium from cocoa supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Chocolate stimulates serotonin production, which can improve mood.

items.title: Lower added sugar
items.content: The absence of icing reduces overall sugar content, making the dessert less sweet overall.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The cookie component typically contains wheat flour, so the product is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Despite lacking icing, brownies remain calorie‑dense due to butter and chocolate.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Dark chocolate contains small amounts of caffeine, which may be undesirable for children or caffeine‑sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Even without frosting, the recipe includes sugar; those with diabetes should monitor portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cookie brownie without icing as a standalone treat, cut into small squares and pair with coffee or tea. It also works well as a base for ice cream, mixed into yogurt, or crumbled over cakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. For longer shelf life (up to 1 month) keep refrigerated. Discard if any mold or off‑odors appear.
